Design prompt · Scope · Sep 18

Raise the UI bar

The earlier sign-in was a small centered Google card. The later Scope screen makes identity and the email action explicit in a restrained approval shell.

Audit → upgrade · visual verificationReal after screenshot, parent/child source comparisoncd0c59c → 7a08d9f

Prompt as used / excerpt

Stay on shadcn components (install more as needed), but raise the visual bar to Stripe/Plaid dashboard quality. That means: clear hierarchy, tight consistent spacing, restrained color with one accent, real empty/loading/error states, and no default-looking cards or walls of sameness. Audit every screen against that bar, list what's below it, then upgrade. Evidence over vibes - name the screen, what's dull, what changed.

03
Architecture · Scope · Sep 19

Scrap the wrong boundary

A slice no longer hangs from a replaceable credential row. Both slices and slice requests point at the stable agent identity.

pstack Architect · Phase E: scrap when wrong · redesign from first principlesExact prompt → exact commit 153c57bf23e7b5 → 153c57b
Prompt as used / excerpt

slices and sliceRequests belong to the agent, not to a credential generation. right now they're keyed by agentConnectionId and activation patches them onto the replacement - that rebind loop is compat scaffolding. bind them to the stable agent lineage, delete the patch loop and the legacy optional field, and activation becomes a pure credential swap. reminder of the 3 rules we work by: scrap when the architecture is wrong, subtract before you add, evidence over taste. the codebase should get smaller, not grow a workaround.

04
Dependency review · Scope · Sep 19

Make dependencies point one way

A dashboard read stopped reaching into slice storage. Slice status and return-path policy moved down to domain owners, and expiry jobs were separated.

pstack-inspired bounded review → fix → re-reviewCycles replaced with domain owners1bcd8a7 → da571a8
Prompt as used / excerpt

Review `<insert_folder>` as one bounded dependency scope. Map its dependency graph. Infer the intended layer direction from each module's responsibility, then state that direction before judging violations. Find every backward dependency edge and every cycle. Include imports that cross the scope boundary when they are needed to explain a coupling, but do not expand this into a repo-wide review. Report a full inventory of every backward edge and cycle you found, with nothing omitted. Rank them by severity. For each one, give: - the dependency path or cycle - file:line evidence for every edge - what the coupling costs in concrete terms: change blast radius, review friction, bug surface, test difficulty, or duplicated logic - the smallest boundary change that would restore one-way dependencies The goal is a codebase that stays maintainable and reviewable over time, so completeness beats brevity here. Do not cap the list or stop at a "worst few". If the inventory is long, keep the per-item format tight instead of dropping entries. Output a written review only. Do not change code. Keep this pass tightly scoped. A focused pass on one folder or tree produces sharper evidence than one diluted repo-wide pass. If more than one area needs review, run this prompt separately for each folder or tree, then compare the reports before deciding what to refactor.

05
Test quality · Scope · Sep 19

Make a test catch a defect

The first refactor removed a shallow provider test, but review caught that the safety invariant was missing. A final follow-up tests all eight providers through POST /api/credentials, demands a 503, and checks that the standing token never appears.

pstack-inspired behavior verificationWeak provider check → real credential endpoint1bcd8a7 → da571a8
Prompt as used / excerpt

Refactor the test suite in <insert_scope> so every test earns its keep: it calls the code the way its users do and asserts a result they observe. Tests exist to catch defects, not to restate the code. The bar for keeping a test: it would fail if the behavior it covers broke. The quick check - if the test would still pass when every function it imports returned undefined, it observes no behavior and cannot fail for a defect.

Open PR ↗Inspect code ↗Reusable prompt ↗

Evidence note: This is not a flawless one-shot result. The final test was restored after human review, in commit da571a8. Both prompts #4 and #5 contributed to PR #40; #5 has a separate test-refactor commit f89ab13.

What held up

Prompt → review → proof.

The UI example has two historical images from different dates, while its commit also changed authentication and branding. The architecture and test runs share PRs with other changes. Every case names that boundary rather than claiming an isolated result it cannot prove.
